chunks: Then two of the men who feared (God), and to whom God was gracious, said to them: "Charge and rush the gate. If you enter, you will surely be victorious. And place your trust in God if you truly believe."

key_terms.أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا: God was gracious to them / to whom God bestowed favor

ai.seo_question: Who were the two men who advised the Israelites to enter the city gate, and what was their message?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, these two men are often identified as Joshua and Caleb, whose counsel to the Israelites highlights the principle of 'Amal al-Mu'tabar' (accepted action) combined with Tawakkul (trust in God). Their advice underscores that spiritual faith must be manifested through decisive physical effort, a theme central to the concept of Jihad al-Akbar (struggle) in Shia tradition.
